result.killer: Not a definitive kill. Main threats: the small market (about 421 licensed accommodation providers per Tourism Fiji, plus about 500 Airbnb listings per the NSTF draft), and planned donor-funded transition support (IFC, Switch Asia/SBDO, Na Vualiku) that is likely to supply free templates and help. Commencement, regulations, fees and any portal are not published (not_reached).
result.reason: I found no product or free state portal that kills this, but none can exist yet: commencement, regulations, fees and forms are all unpublished. Three things weaken it. The market is small: Tourism Fiji counts about 421 licensed accommodation providers, plus roughly 500 Airbnb listings, plus tour operators, so perhaps 1,000-2,000 businesses, many of them micro or village operators who can pay little. Free help is planned: the Minister has named IFC and Switch Asia (through SBDO) assistance for MSMEs and cultural/indigenous tourism enterprises, and the Na Vualiku MSME programme (US$3.2m) already exists. And the Minister says the scheme is a "pathway, not another licence" with a soft transition, while FHTA is pushing for a single window and self-assessment without consultants. A risky, low-revenue, timing-dependent niche.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K14. Minimum wage F$5/hr (reported, from 1 Apr 2025); FNPF registration duty for employees aged 15+. No source specific to households. Employment Relations Act 2007 under revision (unconfirmed).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Scrap Metal Trade Decree/Act 2011 requires a dealer licence (Ministry of Trade; Forms & Fees Regs 2011). Nov 2024 suspension of non-ferrous scrap trade (except gold) and a taskforce (Recycling Today); still in force or not is unconfirmed. Small, enforcement-driven; candidate C05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Fiji second-hand dealers or pawnbroker statute surfaced in the search. Unverified. Not reached beyond one query.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Fiji licensing rule for gold or jewellery buyers found. Only the Nov 2024 non-ferrous scrap suspension, which exempts gold. Unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Fiji-specific dismantler licensing found (only NZ/AU results). The LTA has expanded inspection agencies by outsourcing, which is a separate matter.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K13. Meat Industry Act (Cap 237) governs slaughter, and the Board's 2015 report says the Act is outdated. No livestock-trader register found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Meat Industry Act: meat must come from registered slaughterhouses; rural slaughterhouses need an inspector present (2015 regulation amendment). Food Safety Act health licence applies to butcher shops. No butcher-specific software gap found; candidate C09 (weak).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: BAF Apiculture Movement Application Form (2021) and an AFB surveillance form exist. The 2020 Varroa emergency order has likely lapsed (unconfirmed). Tiny paper-form workflow with a handful of users; candidate C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No Fiji vet-medicine register or reporting rule found. A very small market. Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: The Mineral Resources Dept drills state boreholes. A Groundwater Resources Development and Management Policy and a National Water Resources Management and Sanitation Policy are pending. No driller licence or abstraction licence found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Environment Management Act 2005 plus the 2007 Waste Disposal and Recycling Regulation (Waste Disposal Permit). WAF Liquid Trade Waste Policy covers tankers. 2026 enforcement against a company using an unlicensed transporter. No hauler register or software found; candidate C07 (weak).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1996 (National OHS Service) ties OHS compliance inspection to business licence renewal. No boiler, pressure vessel or lift registration found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: WAF runs urban and most rural supply; no private small-system regulator register found in the search budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: The Pesticides Act 1971 requires every pesticide sold to be registered with the Registrar (Koronivia). The Ministry confiscates unregistered or repacked pesticides from retailers (2023-24). A product register, not a dealer-reporting duty; candidate C08 (weak).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Overseas recruitment agencies need Permanent Secretary authorisation under the Employment Relations Act 2007 and the Employment Agencies Regulations 2008. Very few authorised agencies (April 2026 report). UN CMW has asked about licensing and monitoring. Candidate C04 (weak: tiny buyer base).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: The Burial and Cremation Act is a 1911 law. Burial and Cremation (Amendment) Bill No. 30 of 2025 would modernise licensing of cemeteries and crematoria and raise fines for unlicensed burial from $200 to $5,000; passage not confirmed. The Corrections Service runs many cemeteries. Candidate C06 (weak).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Charitable Trusts Act s.29A requires an annual return with audited accounts; non-filers are cancelled after a Gazette notice (705 organisations listed in 2021). Candidate C01. The Fiji Muslim League runs halal certification and launched a Digital Halal Ecosystem in Oct 2024 with the IsDB, so the halal side is covered; candidate C10b is not needed.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi base/stand reform: K04 (existing operators must secure bases by 30 Sept 2027; permits only to individuals; $30k household income test). New PSV permit transfer ban gazetted 13 March 2026. Bus operators: 53 operators, 1,218 buses, QAMS audits and a bi-annual fleet audit, so the market is too small. Candidates C02, C03.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Municipal market licences (draft 2020 regs: $1,000 a year, $1,500 for fish) and fee waivers are council-run; Cabinet approved stall charges for the new Nakasi Market (Jan 2025). Money changers and Restricted FX Dealers: RBF licensing under the Exchange Control Act, revised operational guidelines (May 2025), reporting to the RBF and FIU. Very few licensees; candidate C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: the LTA cancelled 14 permits in March 2025, stricter instructor rules, about $400 a year renewal per instructor (candidate C03). Food premises health licence renews yearly by January (Food Safety Act 2003, penalty up to $10,000), but the businessNOW FIJI portal handles application and renewal (candidate C12). ECE centres: Ministry of Education approval, 764 to over 1,000 centres (candidate C13). Tattoo: no licence yet, Public Health Act review pending. Hunting outfitters not applicable.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: No fuel/LPG licensing regime found in search. FCCC sets monthly maximum wholesale/retail prices for petroleum and LPG and inspects outlets (adjacent to K05, which is price-control shelf-price compliance for retailers). Service Stations are a VMS (EFD) Phase 3 group under Gazette Notice 61 of 2025 (registration 30 Sep 2025, implementation 31 Dec 2025); service stations are mostly company-run networks (TotalEnergies about 40, Petro Oceania/Mobil over 35), so little of the market is small and quiet. Nothing else new.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Sugar Industry Act (Cap 206) grower registration, with the Sugar Industry Tribunal setting the crushing schedule and Master Award; the Fiji Sugar Corporation manages growers directly, and a 2024 amendment bill on Council elections is unconfirmed. No third-party filing duty for software found. Kava/other commodities covered by K10 (rejected). Nothing new beyond a weak sugar-grower entry.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operatives Act 1996: small co-operatives lodge a streamlined annual return with the Registrar (2020 coops4dev review); the Act was under review in 2020 and a National Co-operative Federation was given an audit/advisory role in 2018. No 2025-26 amendment, current form or co-op count found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: No clinic registration source found. Commercial Health Care is a VMS Phase 3 group (registration 31 Dec 2025, implementation 31 Mar 2026), which is the same duty as K01 (practice-management fiscalization). Free Medicine Programme involves 33 private pharmacies. Nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy Profession Act 2011: only registered pharmacists/private hospital licensees may run pharmacies; Pharmacy Business Authorisation Condition 2 requires a pharmacist present at all times; FCCC audit warned 3 pharmacies for operating without one (maitvfiji). Fiji MRA (under FPBS, MoH) issues a permit for every consignment of pseudoephedrine and approves imported medicines/devices; only licensed importers/wholesalers. Pharmacy POS fiscalization is K07. The pharmacist-roster/authorisation evidence pack idea is weak.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security Industry Act 2010: Security Industry Licensing and Registration Board plus Ministry of Defence; three licence tiers (Master, Individual, Provisional). Law Reform Commission review of the Act began with Commissioner Ana Rokomokoti from 8 June 2026; fewer than 100 of about 3000 security providers are licensed (Fiji Sun). Overseas recruitment agencies need Ministry of Employment authorisation under the Employment Relations Act 2007 and 2008 Agency Regulations, with a $20,000 bond; only about 6 authorised (tiny market). Cleaning agencies not covered by a specific regime found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: No contractor licensing law exists in Fiji (Construction Industry Council task group working on licensing; Master Builders preparing recommendations). Engineers' Registration Board first met 5 Dec 2025 and registration of individual engineers is coming (small, individual professionals). Construction and Real Estate and Architecture & Engineering are VMS groups with a 31 Dec 2025 implementation date (K01-type duty). Building permits are handled by municipal councils. No local-content report regime found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: FTR Act makes lawyers, accountants and real estate agents report suspicious transactions to the FIU and do client due diligence; FIU outreach to the Law Society (Feb 2026) and accountants (Mar 2026). Beneficial-ownership tightening: Cabinet approved Companies Regulations 2015 amendments on 21 Apr 2026, and a Tax Bill (FBC, 28 Jul 2026) proposes a central beneficial-owner register. Current AML thresholds and filing channel not confirmed; the state portal may be free.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism Act 2026 (Act 7 of 2026) repeals the Hotels and Guest Houses Act 1973. Commencement is by Gazette notice (s1(2)); existing operators have 12 months from commencement (s49); s19 requires registration (fine up to $500); application needs TCS classification, a legal compliance declaration listing every applicable law, a tourism criteria self-assessment and a fee (s20-22); 30-day decision; renewal re-declares (s21, s25); a public Tourism Enterprise Register. Definitions cover homestays, village stays, short-term rentals via platforms, camping, houseboats and tourism services. Accommodation is also a VMS group (Group 1 implementation 30 Jun 2026, Group 2 30 Sep 2026). Hotels Licensing Board licences stay valid until replaced (s49(2)). TST is K02.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: BAF issues phytosanitary certificates and export permits; the Fiji Trade Information Portal lists permits by product. No new 2026 traceability rule found. A mahogany shipment is stuck in the UK for lacking certification (Fiji Times, 2026 budget debate) and exporters want FSC/origin certification. Kava is K10 and tuna evidence is K03 (both known).

The Law Reform Commission discussion paper proposes unifying the 3 divisional authorities, with a final report due 30 Oct 2026; FHTA says hotels face an onerous annual renewal. Reform not yet law. See candidate C9.

coverage.category: 36. VAT Monitoring System (EFD) Phase 3 gazetted groups (Gazette Notice 61 of 2025)
coverage.found: FRCS table: Architecture & Engineering, Construction & Real Estate, Service Stations (impl. 31 Dec 2025); Commercial Health Care and Freight Services (31 Mar 2026); Food Services, Accommodation Group 1 (30 Jun 2026); Accommodation Group 2 (30 Sep 2026); Wholesalers, Manufacturers and Retailers (registration 30 Jun 2026, implementation 31 Dec 2026; EFD v2.0 ceases 31 Dec 2026). Applies to turnover of $50,000 or more. See candidates C2-C4.

coverage.category: 37. Workplace OHS compliance for business licences (Health and Safety at Work Act 1996)
coverage.found: The National OHS Service inspects workplaces for business licence renewals (FHTA notice, 2019). No pressure vessel or lift registry found under Fiji law. Low priority; see candidate C10.

result.competitor: I found no vendor, consultant pack or state portal (3 searches covering portal, consultant/self-assessment and regulations). The forms and criteria have not been published, so nothing can exist yet. Risks: FHTA is publicly lobbying for a 'single-window' coordinated system and for a self-assessment pathway that small operators can complete 'without consultants'. The Ministry is therefore likely to issue free templates or an online form. The Act also lets third-party certification and verifiers be accepted. I did not run iTaukei or Hindi searches because the business language is English.
result.duty: The Tourism Act 2026 (Act No. 7 of 2026) has been enacted and replaces the Hotel and Guest Houses Act 1973. Its table of contents lists s19 requirement for registration, s20 application, s21 legal compliance declaration, s22 tourism criteria self-assessment, s23 Recognition Certificate, plus renewal, tier progression, suspension/cancellation and acceptable verifiers. Press reports confirm that all tourism businesses must apply to the Ministry of Tourism using a prescribed form, a classification, a legal compliance declaration, a self-assessment and a fee. The Ministry has 30 days to decide, and approved businesses are listed on a public Tourism Enterprise Register. Coverage includes hotels, tour operators, community-based tourism, camping/hiking and Airbnb-type short-term rentals. NOT confirmed (the Act PDF and Bill PDF would not extract through WebFetch): the commencement date or gazette notice, the $500 fine, the renewal frequency, and the 12-month transition for existing operators. FHTA (5 June 2026) says the Act is 'not at the finish line yet' and that forms, fees, criteria, tiers and timelines are left to regulations not yet made. I found no regulations or consultation as of Oct 2026. Separately, the Tourism Services Tax Act 2026 (Act 20) has been in force since 1 Sep 2026. That is a different duty.
result.market: This is small. A draft National Sustainable Tourism Framework (cited by the Fiji Times) counts 400+ licensed accommodation providers, notes that this undercounts the total, and cites 500+ Airbnb listings. I found no counts of tour operators or village stays. A plausible total of registrants is roughly 1,000-2,000 businesses, many of them micro or community operators with low ability to pay. FBoS data: 13,249 paid employees in licensed accommodation (Q1 2026).
result.reason: The registration duty is real in the enacted Act, but it cannot be acted on yet. The commencement date, renewal cycle, fees, forms and self-assessment criteria all depend on regulations that are unpublished as of Oct 2026, so the claim's specifics (fine of $500, 12-month transition) are unverified. The market is tiny (about 400 licensed accommodation providers plus Airbnb hosts and tour operators). Many are village or community operators with low willingness to pay. FHTA is pushing for a single-window system and a pathway small operators can complete without consultants, so a free Ministry form or template is likely. The opportunity is best treated as a one-off filing-assistance service once the regulations land. Revisit when the regulations are gazetted.

The duty is real. Charitable Trusts Act s.29A (2013) requires a yearly return to the Registrar of Titles with trustee and office-bearer names and audited accounts. If a trust doesn't file, the Registrar must cancel its incorporation unless there were good reasons. Cancellation follows Gazette and newspaper notices. The Registrar may also publish the names of non-compliant trusts. 705 organisations were cancelled for not submitting accounts by 31 Dec 2021. I found no filing software, and no online filing portal. The sources I searched don't say how returns are submitted, so I could not check this. I could not find a count of registered trusts. Weak points: the buyers are volunteer-run, the real cost is the audit, which software does not remove, willingness to pay is low, and the market is small. Whether s.29A is still unamended was not checked against a current consolidated Act.

The duty is real. LTA regulations gazetted 13 March 2026 stop PSV permit transfers by sale. Transfers are allowed only for family, migration, medical incapacity or death, and pending transfers are not processed. This is a one-off rule change, not a recurring filing. The only recurring duty I found is permit re-issue, which an undated Fiji Times piece says must be applied for at least 28 days before expiry. That is a low-frequency, low-pain task. Market is about 8,800 permits nationwide (Oct 2023 Cabinet figure, not broken down by type). That is small, fragmented and unlikely to pay for software. I found no competing software. I did not check LTA's website, the gazette text or penalties. The tracker would be thin.

result.reason: The duty is real. The FRCS Phase 3 page (frcs.org.fj/?p=27312) gives Accommodation Group 1 registration 31 Mar 2026 and implementation 30 Jun 2026, and Group 2 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026. It covers turnover of $50,000 and above, and businesses under $100,000 can ask the CEO for relief. I found no penalty text, and Gazette Notice 61 of 2025 was not checked. The "nothing does the core job" part fails. Counterpoint's CP VMS middleware is FRCS-accredited under Hospitality (fhta.com.fj), with Hotel Link as the named PMS. Counterpoint invites other PMS users to ask about compatibility. Datec's iVend is also accredited, and was used at Musket Cove. A bridge for other PMS products or spreadsheets remains possible but is a thin niche. Both deadlines have passed. The FRCS vendor list and the market count were not found.

Duty is real: FRCS page (Gazette Notice 61/2025) lists Phase 3 sectors with EFD/VMS Version 3.0 dates (A&E, construction, real estate 31 Dec 2025; health care and freight 31 Mar 2026; food services 30 Jun 2026, corrected). It applies at turnover of $50,000 or more. The page fetched does not state penalties. Competition: FRCS keeps an accredited POS & SDC list, with a V3 list updated 1 Jun 2026, so accredited vendors already do the core job. I could not read the vendor table. The deadlines mostly passed by Oct 2026, so the urgency window is closing. Market size was not found. Same core duty as K01, so the earlier rejection stands. No sector gap was shown.

Duty confirmed: the FRCS notice lists Service Stations in the first Phase 3 group (registration 30 Sep 2025, implementation 31 Dec 2025, Gazette Notice 61 of 2025). It applies to businesses with turnover of $50k or more. Both dates have passed. The notice doesn't state penalties. Competition: FRCS runs an accredited POS/SDC vendor list, with local vendors such as Link Technologies and Tech 360, and vendors had to re-accredit for v3. Fuel retail is dominated by majors with their own systems, and independents are few. I found no outlet count and no fuel-specific vendor. I couldn't confirm LPG dealer coverage. A solo founder would also have to pass FRCS accreditation. The window has closed and the buyer pool is tiny, so the score is low. This is a duplicate of K07.

Cabinet approved amendments to the Companies Regulations 2015 on 21 Apr 2026, and an FBC report of 28 Jul 2026 says the Tax Bill would add a central beneficial-owner register. Neither source gives a final rule, commencement date, deadline, filing body, penalty or frequency. The Fiji Times article has none of these, and the FIU page returned a 503. I found no evidence the rule is in force. A commercial blog says beneficial ownership information is filed with the Registrar, but it is unconfirmed. The register will probably be a free state portal, and the duty looks like a one-off or event-driven filing, so a standalone product is weak. I found no competitor, but I didn't search deeply. I found no firm count; the company register would supply it. A better angle is a helper for accountants and company secretaries once the rules are gazetted. Recheck then.
